title: MetadataChangesParams.extra: serde_json::Map exposed in public API
description:
src/methods/mod.rs:60 — 'pub extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>' exposes the serde_json types in the public API surface. If serde_json cuts a major version (it has not in ~6 years, but the contract risk is real), this crate's API breaks.

Mitigations:
(a) Pin serde_json explicitly in this crate's Cargo.toml at the same major version the workspace uses, and document.
(b) Wrap with a local newtype 'pub struct VendorExtras(serde_json::Map<…>)' — verbose, fights the workspace extras-preservation policy that explicitly normalises on serde_json::Map.
(c) Accept the risk and document in README 'Gotchas' that this crate's API depends on serde_json's stability.

The workspace AGENTS.md 'Extras-preservation policy' already standardises on serde_json::Map<String, Value> as the canonical extras type. Changing this crate alone would diverge from policy. So (a) and (c) are the realistic paths.

Recommendation: (c). This is a known and accepted dependency on serde_json's stability — it ships in essentially every Rust web crate and a major version bump would break the entire ecosystem in lockstep. Document the dependency explicitly so a future downstream that wants to vendor 'jmap-metadata-client' on a different serde_json major knows the constraint.

Workspace-wide: every *-client and *-types crate has the same exposure. Propagate the README documentation.

Marked opinion: bordering on bikeshedding given how stable serde_json has been. Filing conservatively because the contract decision fossilises at 0.1.0.
